title: Summit Biosystems - Renewal & Regional Burst Alignment
summary: Customer is approaching renewal window; wants to add burst capacity for a seasonal campaign, onboard EU region, and extend contract by 12 months. Key concerns: data residency, SOC2 scope, and predictable latency for peak inference. Action items and SOW amendment required.
action_items: Mateo Ruiz | Draft amended SOW with 12-month extension + burst clause | 2026-02-12
Samir Patel | Run quick perf benchmark for current model on EU region and share latency report | 2026-02-10
Elena Park | Share SOC2 and data residency docs and escalate legal questions to support | 2026-02-08
Rafael Ortiz | Provide expected Q2 traffic profile (rps, peak minutes) | 2026-02-07
next_steps: Mateo to send SOW + pricing options
Schedule 60-min perf deep dive with Rafael and Samir next week
Customer to confirm sign-off stakeholders by 2026-02-09
Legal to review amended terms and flag any changes needed to indemnity/data residency clauses
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-05 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Mateo Ruiz (Redwood AE); Elena Park (Redwood CSM); Samir Patel (Redwood SE); Alyssa Chen (CTO, Summit Biosystems); Rafael Ortiz (Head of MLOps); Priya Nambiar (Legal); Derrick Lowe (SRE)

00:00 - Mateo: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick agenda — renewal window is coming up, we want to talk burst add-on for your Q2 campaign and EU region onboarding, plus any contract tweaks.
00:22 - Alyssa: Yep thanks, Mateo. We're basically looking at two things: the seasonality spike in April/May and moving some inference into EU for data residency. Also want to make sure any extension doesn't change our compliance posture.
00:40 - Elena: Great. Just to call out, we tracked the usage pattern you sent last week, Rafael — looks like a 3x peak for ~48 hours during your simulated runs?
00:50 - Rafael: Uh, yeah roughly. There was, um, the weekend test where we saw up to 3.4x but sustained for closer to 36 hours in our latest sim. So need headroom and quick ramp.
01:05 - Samir: For burst we've got two levers: reserved baseline + burst pool, or autoscaling with fast warm GPU pool. Baseline keeps latency tighter under normal load, burst lets you absorb spikes but cost is higher per minute.
01:25 - Derrick: Latency is non-negotiable for some endpoints. We can't have more than 120ms p95 for our customer-facing scoring calls. Does Redwood guarantee that during burst?
01:35 - Mateo: We set SLOs per route; for burst we'll propose a reserved+burst config. The reserved guarantees capacity for core traffic and the burst pool is best-effort but we can add a fallback to a lighter quantized model to keep latency within budget.
01:50 - Priya: On the contract side, any fallback that touches data residency or changes where inference runs, we need that documented — also SOC2 scope must remain the same.
02:05 - Elena: Noted. We'll flag any region changes in the SOW. For EU onboarding we have two paths: hosted EU region under Redwood control, or Private VPC with customer-managed networking. Which are you leaning to?
02:18 - Alyssa: Prefer hosted EU if it meets residency because it's simpler, but our legal wants the option for Private if we need tighter controls.
02:28 - Priya: Exactly. Also need to know KMS/HSM options for keys — our security team requires key management integration for model inputs retention.
02:40 - Samir: We support KMS integrations — Google, AWS, also bring-your-own keys via HSM in the Private deployment. For hosted EU, keys can be customer-controlled with KMS and we can ensure logs are stored in EU.
02:55 - Rafael: How long to spin up EU nodes for the reserved+burst config? If we commit now, what's the lead time?
03:05 - Mateo: Typical lead time is 6–8 weeks for dedicated reserved capacity in a new region, shorter (2–3 weeks) if we can use existing multi-tenant hosted pool. But burst-only setups can be faster, like 1–2 weeks to enable autoscale on hosted.
03:20 - Alyssa: That lead time is... tight for us. Our campaign starts mid-April, so we need provisioned EU by early April ideally.
03:30 - Mateo: Okay if you need early April, we should go hosted EU with autoscale enabled now and then migrate to dedicated reserved capacity by May if numbers justify it.
03:45 - Rafael: That could work. What's the expected delta in cost between hosted autoscale and reserved capacity? Ballpark.
03:55 - Samir: Ballpark, hosted autoscale is about 1.8–2.5x per-minute cost on burst traffic versus reserved amortized over the month. Exact depends on hours used, GPU type; I'll run an estimate with your traffic profile.
04:10 - Elena: We'll include both pricing options in the SOW so you can choose.
04:18 - Priya: For legal — indemnity and data residency clauses: we need a line that processing for EU customers remains in EU, and a clause for audit access. Are you able to accept that?
04:30 - Mateo: We can include region-residency commitments and an audit logs access plan in the SOW. I'll flag with legal.
04:40 - Alyssa: Also, what about model fallback quality? If you route to quantized model under burst, we need to ensure the scoring differences are within an acceptable margin. We'll need a validation run.
04:53 - Samir: Totally. We can run a side-by-side eval with your golden test set — show quality delta and latency improvements. That's part of the perf deep dive.
05:05 - Rafael: Can we also test prefix caching for repeated requests? A lot of our workload reuses prefixes and that could save cost/latency.
05:15 - Samir: Yes, we have prefix/KV caching. We'll include recommendations: TTLs, cache warmer patterns, and the expected token savings for your workload.
05:25 - Alyssa: Next, about the extension length. We're thinking 12 months, but want a 60-day window for adjustments if usage deviates significantly in Q3.
05:35 - Mateo: We can do a 12-month term with quarterly usage review and an adjustment clause — essentially a committed baseline with a ramp schedule. I'll draft the wording.
05:45 - Priya: On pricing, any early-payment or commit discounts? If we sign for 12 months and commit to X GPU-hours, what's the uplift?
05:55 - Mateo: We can propose tiered discounts based on committed baseline. I'll put three tiers in the SOW: baseline-only, baseline+burst, baseline+dedicated reserve. Each with pricing and penalty/credits for overages.
06:10 - Alyssa: Good. Also, can Redwood provide a stub SOW now just so our procurement has something to review while legal spins?
06:18 - Elena: Yes we'll send a stub with the proposed numbers and the key clauses — privacy, residency, SSO/SAML, KMS options.
06:28 - Priya: For SSO, we use Okta and need SCIM for user provisioning. Confirm Redwood supports that.
06:35 - Samir: SCIM and SAML SSO are supported; I'll add the Okta integration notes to the security pack.
06:45 - Rafael: About monitoring — we need token-level cost breakdown and model-level latency dashboards. Can Redwood expose that to our team?
06:53 - Elena: Yes, Redwood Console provides per-route dashboards and you can create API keys with read-only view for your dashboarding. We can also send daily CSV exports if needed.
07:05 - Derrick: Any outage/failover behavior documented? Our stack needs graceful degradation to a lower-cost path if a region becomes unhealthy.
07:15 - Mateo: We'll add failover policy: automatic routing to alternate region with notice and ability to pin to specific model variants. Also SLA credit details will be in the SOW.
07:30 - Alyssa: Ok so to recap, main asks: hosted EU enablement asap, reserved baseline + burst, 12-month extension with quarterly reviews and optional migration to dedicated capacity in May, perf benchmarks and quantized fallback validation, and legal to review residency language.
07:50 - Mateo: Yep. I'll action the SOW and pricing, Samir will run the perf report and caching analysis, Elena will send the security pack. Rafael to share traffic profile. Priya will coordinate legal review.
08:05 - Priya: Quick question — if we go hosted EU, will data egress charges be different? I need the ballpark.
08:12 - Samir: Egress follows cloud provider pricing; we'll include a rough estimate. If you go private, egress is mostly internal to your VPC so different.
08:22 - Alyssa: Anything from competitors we should be aware of? Rafael did a bake-off with Mallory AI — they offered a dedicated EU node but no KV cache; CloudX had cheaper burst costs but worse latency.
08:36 - Mateo: Good context, thanks. We'll make sure our SOW highlights caching and predictable latency as differentiators.
08:45 - Elena: Final thing — timeline. Can everyone confirm dates? Rafael to send profile by Feb 7, Samir to return perf report by Feb 10, Mateo to send draft SOW by Feb 12, legal to aim review by Feb 19, and next call for perf deep dive the week of Feb 16.
09:05 - Rafael: Confirmed.
09:07 - Priya: Confirmed.
09:10 - Mateo: Great, we should be able to hit the early April target with hosted EU turned on if we move quickly. Thanks all.

End of transcript.

Notes: Transcript contains natural speech patterns and occasional filler. Some proper nouns may be transcribed imperfectly.
